tests.title: IsReady follows depends_on, an explicit empty list, and the previous-task default
given: a plan of four tasks: task 1 pending without depends_on, task 2 pending without depends_on, task 3 pending with depends_on [], task 4 pending with depends_on [1,2]
task 1 is done and task 2 is pending
tests.when: IsReady is called for ids 1, 2, 3 and 4, and again after task 1 is set to in_progress
then: with task 1 done: IsReady(2) is true because the previous task is done
IsReady(3) is true because an explicit empty list means no dependencies
IsReady(4) is false because task 2 is not done
IsReady(1) is false because task 1 is done and not pending
a pending first task without depends_on is ready
a pending task whose previous task is in_progress is not ready
tests.pseudocode: p = plan(...); assert p.IsReady(2); assert p.IsReady(3); assert !p.IsReady(4); assert !p.IsReady(1)

tests.title: A missing or dropped dependency makes the task not ready
given: task 2 pending with depends_on [99]
task 3 pending with depends_on [1] where task 1 is dropped
task 4 pending without depends_on whose previous task 3 is dropped
tests.when: IsReady is called for tasks 2, 3 and 4
then: IsReady returns false for each of the three tasks
tests.pseudocode: assert !p.IsReady(2); assert !p.IsReady(3); assert !p.IsReady(4)

tests.title: IsReady returns false for an unknown id or a nil receiver without panicking
given: a plan with tasks 1 and 2
a nil *TasksV2Json
tests.when: IsReady(42), IsReady(0), IsReady(-1) are called on the plan and IsReady(1) on the nil receiver
then: every call returns false
no call panics
tests.pseudocode: var n *TasksV2Json; assert !n.IsReady(1); assert !p.IsReady(42)

tests.title: NextTask returns a copy of the first in_progress task
given: a plan where task 2 and task 3 are in_progress and task 1 is done, task 4 pending and ready-looking
tests.when: NextTask is called and the returned task's Title and DependsOn are mutated
then: it returns (task 2, true)
the plan's task 2 title and depends_on are unchanged after the mutation
tests.pseudocode: t, ok = p.NextTask(); assert ok && t.Id == 2; t.Title = 'x'; assert p.Tasks[1].Title != 'x'

tests.title: NextTask returns the first ready task when none is in progress
given: a plan where task 1 is done, task 2 is dropped, task 3 is pending with depends_on [1], task 4 is pending with depends_on [3]
then: it returns (task 3, true)
tests.pseudocode: t, ok = p.NextTask(); assert ok && t.Id == 3

tests.title: NextTask returns (nil, false) for a nil plan, an empty plan, and a blocked plan
given: a nil receiver
a plan with no tasks
a plan where every task is done or dropped
a plan where the only pending task depends on an unfinished pending task that is itself blocked
then: each call returns nil and false
no call panics
tests.pseudocode: for p in cases: t, ok = p.NextTask(); assert t == nil && !ok

tests.title: examples/tasks pick with id 0 uses NextTask and keeps its two messages
given: a plan fully done or dropped
a plan whose only pending task has an unfinished dependency
a plan with an in_progress task and one with a ready pending task
tests.when: pick(tasks, 0) is called on each, and the existing examples/tasks tests are run
then: the fully done plan fails with an error containing "every task is done or dropped"
the blocked plan fails with an error containing "no pending task has all its dependencies done"
the in_progress task is chosen first, otherwise the first ready task
the existing examples/tasks tests pass unchanged
tests.pseudocode: _, err = pick(done, 0); assert contains(err, 'every task is done or dropped')

tests.title: NextTask returns the first in_progress task, else the earliest ready task
given: generated plans with random states, random present, absent or empty depends_on, and ids that may dangle
tests.when: for any task plan, NextTask is called
then: when it returns (t, true) and some task is in_progress, t is the first in_progress task in plan order
when it returns (t, true) and none is in progress, IsReady(t.Id) is true and no earlier task is ready
when it returns false, no task is in_progress and no task is ready
tests.pseudocode: for p in gen_plans(): t, ok = p.NextTask(); if ok: if any(inprog): assert t.Id == first_inprog.Id else: assert p.IsReady(t.Id) and not any(p.IsReady(x.Id) for x in before(t)) else: assert none inprog and none ready

tests.title: The shared resolver resolves paths, names, numbers and reaches archived packages only by path
given: a repo with .specs/01_a, .specs/09_b and .specs/archive/09_old
the working directory is the repo root and --dir is set
tests.when: the resolver is called with a package directory path, a file path inside it, a path relative to --dir, the directory name, the number, the bare name, and the path of the archived package
then: each live reference returns the absolute package directory
a number reference 09 resolves to 09_b, not the archived 09_old
the archive path resolves to the archived directory
results equal those of the former specr locate
tests.pseudocode: d = specpkg.Locate('speca', ref, root, specsDir); assert d == abs('.specs/09_b')

tests.title: The resolver refuses bad references with a usage error naming the calling tool
given: a repo with .specs/09_b and an archived .specs/archive/05_old
tests.when: the resolver is called with tool "specr" and "speca" and references -, https://example.com/x, a multi-line string, an unknown name, an ambiguous reference matching two packages, and the number 05
then: each call returns a *cli.UsageError whose Category() is "usage"
each message begins with the tool name passed in
for 05 the message names the archived package that matches
tests.pseudocode: err = Locate('speca', '-', ...); assert errors.As(err, &ue) && ue.Category()=='usage' && startsWith(err.Error(), 'speca')

tests.title: The listing returns NN_name directories and the display rule picks relative or absolute
given: a root holding 01_a, 10_b, notes.txt, a directory named misc, and archive/
a --dir containing the root, and a package path outside --dir
tests.when: the directory listing and the display rule are called
then: only NN_name directories are returned
a path inside --dir is shown relative to it
a path outside --dir is shown absolute
tests.pseudocode: assert names(List(root)) == ['01_a','10_b']; assert Display(inside, dir) == '.specs/01_a'; assert Display(outside, dir) == outside

tests.title: The task summary builds TaskInfo in plan order with a copied depends_on and ready
given: a plan with a done task, a ready pending task, a blocked pending task and an optional task
tests.when: the task summary builder is called, then the returned depends_on is mutated

ready is true only for the ready pending task
mutating TaskInfo.DependsOn leaves the plan unchanged
tests.pseudocode: infos = specpkg.TaskInfos(spec); assert [i.ID for i in infos] == ids; assert infos[1].Ready && !infos[2].Ready

tests.title: The moved converters produce the same validation and traceability reports as before and spec output is unchanged
given: a fixture package with errors, warnings, uncovered criteria and an unowned test
the golden output captured from the pre-move specgen conversion
tests.when: specpkg converts the ValidationResult and the spec's traceability, and specgen runs the pipeline over the same package
then: ValidationReport has valid, error_count, warning_count and items with check, artifact, entity, message
TraceReport has criteria_covered, criteria_uncovered, paths_covered, paths_uncovered, tests_unowned
the JSON of spec's result is byte-for-byte equal to the golden output
specgen no longer defines reportOf, itemOf, traceOf, unownedTests

tests.title: Rule names are the distinct Check, or Category when Check is empty, in first-appearance order
given: entries with Check values C3, C7, C3, an entry with empty Check and Category schema, and one with Category cross_spec_actor and Check cross_spec_actor
tests.when: the rule-names function is called, and called on an empty set
then: it returns [C3, C7, schema, cross_spec_actor]
an empty set returns an empty result

tests.title: specr output is unchanged except for ready, and its schema golden includes ready
given: a repo with the 09_agent_mode and 01_test_feature fixtures
tests.when: specr renders a package, a task with --task N, and --schema, and the cmd/specr tests run
then: each entry of result.tasks and result.task carries ready
all other result fields match the previous behaviour
cmd/specr/testdata/schema.golden.json contains ready on TaskInfo and the golden test passes

tests.title: speca writes exactly one speca envelope and accepts flags before or after the input

tool is "speca"
the process exit code equals env.exit_code
flag order before or after the input gives the same result

tests.title: -h and --help print the help to stderr with the sibling sentence and exit 0

tests.title: A bare invocation prints help and exits 2 with a usage envelope when stdout is not a terminal

then: exit code 2

stdout holds one usage envelope with exit_code 2

tests.title: --version prints speca and the build identity
given: a known build identity
then: stdout is "speca <identity>"
exit code 0

tests.title: --schema matches the checked-in golden file without reading any directory
given: a nonexistent --dir and input
then: exit code 0
stdout equals cmd/speca/testdata/schema.golden.json
the document holds tool, description with the sibling sentence, input with examples, flags, result without side_effects, input, model and usage, and exit_codes
UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 rewrites the golden file

tests.title: Every malformed invocation exits 2 with a usage envelope and no result
given: a repo with .specs/09_agent_mode and another package sharing a number or name prefix for an ambiguous reference
tests.when: Main is run with: two inputs; `--list 09`; `--validate --list`; `--all 09`; `-`; a URL; a multi-line input; --dir pointing to a file; reference `99` naming no package; an ambiguous reference; and --bogus

tests.title: speca writes no file and ignores credential and model environment variables

tests.title: valid is always present, failing_rules appears only when invalid, and no spec_invalid warning is raised

both exit 0

tests.title: intent_drift is true only for an active package whose intent no longer matches

a draft package with a mismatching hash
an active package with no intent_hash

tests.title: The report lists tasks with counts and the next task

tests.title: An unreadable spec root omits dependents and raises a low specs_dir_unreadable warning

every other field is reported

tests.title: A package in another format version is reported with a high spec_invalid warning

tests.title: --validate returns identity, verdict, validation and traceability only

then: exit 0
result has the identity fields, intent_drift when true, valid, validation and traceability
tasks, task_counts, next_task, allowed_status, depends_on, dependents and failing_rules are absent
result.valid equals validation.valid equals (error_count == 0)

tests.title: --validate keeps only the cross-spec findings attributed to the package
given: packages A, B and C where A names an unknown dependency, B has a cross_spec_actor error, C defines a glossary term conflicting with B, and A and B are on a dependency cycle

cross-spec findings come after the package's own findings

tests.title: --validate skips cross-spec rules when the spec root cannot be read

tests.title: --list sorts packages by numeric prefix, with ties broken by full name

tests.title: --all appends archived packages marked archived and tolerates a missing archive

tests.title: --list on an unreadable or missing spec root fails at load with a --specs-dir hint

tests.title: The list summary gives the package count, non-zero status counts in lifecycle order and unreadable count

given: the schema encoder is replaced by one that returns an error
then: exit 1
stdout holds one envelope with error.stage "schema" and error.category "internal"
result is absent
tests.pseudocode: encode = failing; code = Main(['--schema'],out,err); assert code==1 && env.Error.Stage=='schema' && env.Error.Category=='internal'

tests.title: An agent reads a package's state and follows the suggested specr call
given: a repo with v2_example under .specs/09_agent_mode and valid_spec_with_arch under .specs/01_test_feature
the spec and specr commands' real Main entry points
tests.when: speca 09 is run from the repo root, then specr is run with the suggested next input and flags
then: speca exits 0 with one envelope holding the package state, tasks with ready, next_task and allowed_status
next holds one entry specr <spec_dir> --task N
running that call returns a RenderResult whose task carries ready and N as id
no file in the repo changed
tests.pseudocode: e1 = speca('09'); n = e1.Next[0]; e2 = specr(n.Input, n.Flags); assert e2.Result.Task.ID == e1.Result.NextTask.ID

tests.title: An agent asks for the full verdict on a package under a root with sibling packages
given: a repo with several packages, one depending on another, one with a cross-spec actor error
real Validate and ValidateCrossSpec
then: exit 0
one envelope with valid false, validation listing the package's own and kept cross-spec findings, and traceability
summary names the error count and rule names
no tasks field and no file changed
tests.pseudocode: env = speca(pkg,'--validate'); assert code==0 && !*env.Result.Valid && contains(env.Summary, 'does not validate')

tests.title: An agent lists every package including the archive
given: a repo with live packages in several states, one malformed package, and archive/ holding a superseded package
then: exit 0
packages are in numeric order with the archived package at the end marked archived: true
the malformed package has load_error only
summary has per-status counts and the unreadable count
next suggests specr <spec_dir> --task N for the first active package with a ready task and none in progress
tests.pseudocode: env = speca('--list','--all'); assert env.Result.Packages[-1].Archived; assert env.Next[0].Tool=='specr'

tests.title: A positional input with --list is refused before anything is read
given: a repo with .specs/09_agent_mode and a snapshot of its file tree
tests.when: the speca binary's Main is run with `--list 09`
then: exit 2
stderr holds the message
stdout holds one usage envelope with stage usage and category usage and no result
the file tree is unchanged
tests.pseudocode: code = Main(['--list','09'], out, err); assert code==2 && env.Error.Stage=='usage' && err != ''
